speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with a skin lesion on your chest; can you describe exactly what it looks like, including its color, size, and if it is painful, bleeding, or changing appearance?

To help me understand better, how long has this lesion been present, and have you noticed any similar spots elsewhere on your body?

Finally, do you have any history of sunburns, recent trauma to the area, or a personal/family history of skin cancer?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Melanoma

Based on your report of a lesion on the chest that has increased in size over two months in a 63-year-old male, this warrants urgent investigation. I am requesting an examination and a biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest skin lesion photograph. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy_Chest_lesion.
